[Description of non-text elements:]
The page is a title page featuring an elaborate woodcut border. The border includes architectural columns, decorative foliage, and various figures: winged putti at the top, portrait medallions on the sides, and siren-like figures at the bottom corners. The central illustration depicts a 16th-century printing workshop with figures operating a manual press. The printed text uses both black and red ink. Several handwritten annotations in ink are present on the page.

For the `p` with a stroke, I'll use `ꝑ` (p with stroke through descender) if possible, or just `p` with a note. I'll try to find the unicode. `ꝑ` is U+A751. `ꝓ` is U+A753 (p with flourish for 'pro'). In this text, it's the 'pro' abbreviation.

Let's re-read the first paragraph again.
`pculdubio` -> `ꝓculdubio`
`pfeſſoribus` -> `ꝓfeſſoribus`
`pprimū` -> `ꝓprimū`
Actually, looking at `pfeſſoribus`, the stroke is through the descender, which usually means `per`. But `profeſſoribus` is the word.
In `pprimū`, the first `p` has a stroke through the descender, the second is normal. `ꝓprimū`? No, it's `proprium`.
I will just use `p` and note the stroke if it's not a standard character I can easily type. I'll use `p` and `q;` etc.

**ASCENSIVS.**

Aut crimina impingam. Putem scribendum esse: At crimina &c. In Politianū. credam redundare in. Magis re
natę q̄ restitutę &c. Renascuntur literæ Romanæ dum ex iisdem fontibus videlicet græcis quasi ex eadem matre no
uæ sed similes veteribus exhauriuntur. Restituuntur autem dum semel natę atq inuentę in pristinum statum pul
sis erroribus & mendis reponuntur. Cum ergo græcos authores minetur se emissurum, latinas literas ex illis ori
turas autumat.

- `ꝙ` (q with a tail) = que
- `⁹` (superscript 9) = us

- `q̄` = qui/quae/quam

- `&` = et
- `ę` = ae

- `Nā` = Nam

γασέρα δ' οὔπως ἔστιν ἀποκρύψαι μεμαυῖαν. Ventrem vero non licet tegere furentem.
Affectiones quoque eas quæ πάθη dicantur a græcis, omnis Homerus circa cor ipsum constituit, vt
iram, κραδίη δέ οἱ ἔνδον ὑλάκτει. (.i. cor aut ipsi intus latrat)

rodis animum?)

pectus exilit, subtremunt aut fortia membra)
Audacia postremo: vt καρδίη ἄλληκτον πολεμίζειν ἠδὲ μάχεσθαι (.i. corde incessanter bellare & pugnare)
Inde illud est, qd Stoicorum opinio principatu cordi potissimu tribuit. Quod bene aut Homerus etia causas
explicat affectionum: Iram quippe ex animi mœrore oriri, effervescente circa cor, vel sanguine, vel
